definitions.applicability: A provisional explicit meaning used to construct and test one product epoch while learning may still revise the term.

scientific_formal.normative_statement: A Definition Prototype is a versioned, source-bound, challengeable meaning hypothesis for one construction epoch. It states scope, exclusions, boundaries, tests, and residue, may be revised without an authority decision before candidate freeze, and always has authority effect none.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: DefinitionPrototype(d,e) = (id, version, meaning, scope, exclusions, tests, sources, residue); authority_effect(d)=none; revise(d) => new_epoch_or_version(d), not admission(d).
boundary_conditions: Version and construction epoch are explicit.
Revision never implies admission.
Prototype posture is machine-checkable.
testable_conditions: Source bindings and non-collapse boundaries resolve.

plain_language.explanation: A Definition Prototype is the current best explicit meaning used to build and learn. It can change as the prototype teaches us more.

domain_context.explanation: CML08-P0 uses these records to make the first Craft vertical buildable without putting unfinished meanings into the Lab authority registry.

boundaries: Definition Prototype is not an admitted Definition.
Validation of its shape is not semantic promotion.
A later canonical Definition may preserve, revise, split, reclassify, collapse, or drop it.

four_facets.human_projection: generated explanation with three colocated voices

definitions.applicability: A provisional graph-like navigation aid connecting exact prototype concepts, relations, source selectors, evidence, questions, and challenge routes for agents.

scientific_formal.normative_statement: An Agent-Facing Ontology Scaffold is a non-authoritative, versioned navigation projection over exact prototype sources. Its nodes and relation hints help agents locate and trace construction material but cannot establish truth, admission, permission, or a reason to block work outside its declared dependencies.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: Scaffold(s)=(sources,nodes,hints,questions,evidence,challenges); authority_effect(s)=none; hint(s,a,b) =/=> canonical_relation(a,b); drift(x) blocks only if x in selected_dependencies(s).

notation.meaning: A provisional relation aid, not an admitted semantic edge.

boundary_conditions: Every source is exact and selected.
Every relation is marked prototype-hint.
Ambient drift outside selected dependencies is diagnostic only.
testable_conditions: No scaffold validation result grants admission.

plain_language.explanation: The scaffold is a map for agents. It helps them find and connect prototype material, but the map is not the territory or an approval gate.

domain_context.explanation: CML08-P1 will project these prototype terms into a navigation scaffold after P0 passes; the suspended Python ontology runtime will not own or gate it.

boundaries: Ontology Scaffold is not canonical truth or semantic authority.
Scaffold currentness is not product approval.
A scaffold cannot widen its selected dependency set implicitly.

four_facets.schema: versioned scaffold with exact sources and hints

definitions.applicability: A provisional statement of one outcome the Craft Product may need to enable, used to construct and test the first thin vertical.

scientific_formal.normative_statement: A Product Capability Prototype is a versioned hypothesis of a Product-owned outcome, participants, consumers, scope, exclusions, contracts, context policies, evidence route, and challenge route. It specializes CAV2-D67 for learning but is not adopted and selects no realization or permission.

notation.meaning: One provisional Product Capability outcome contract.

boundary_conditions: Exactly one Product anchor is explicit.
Outcome and exclusions are testable.
Realization and instance identities remain separate.
testable_conditions: Product Feature and Product Capability IDs cannot collapse.
Capability Instance has a separate ID.
No adoption or authority field is inferred.

plain_language.explanation: This is our current testable guess about what useful outcome Craft must enable, before deciding that the capability is final or adopted.

domain_context.explanation: The first Craft prototype may explore System Construction, but the existing Product Feature name does not silently create this capability identity.

boundaries: Product Capability Prototype is not Product Feature.
Product Capability Prototype is not Capability Instance.
A working implementation does not adopt the capability.

definitions.applicability: The minimal provisional concepts, relations, rules, constraints, and language required to test one Product Capability Prototype.

scientific_formal.normative_statement: A Capability-Local Business Ontology Prototype is an exact, bounded, provisional semantic closure for one Product Capability Prototype and declared context posture. It contains only meanings needed to state and test that outcome and remains revisable and non-authoritative.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: BOP(c,e)=(concepts,relations,rules,constraints,language,sources,residue); closure(BOP) subset required_meaning(c); authority_effect(BOP)=none; BOP =/= SystemOntology.

notation.meaning: The Product Capability Prototype it serves.

boundary_conditions: Exactly one capability prototype is named.
Unselected ambient ontology material is excluded.
Context-local terms preserve their owning boundary.
testable_conditions: Every node supports a named capability obligation.
Business and system ontology identities remain distinct.

plain_language.explanation: This is the smallest shared model of the business meaning needed to test one capability—not a universal ontology of everything nearby.

domain_context.explanation: CML09-P2 will build this closure only after the provisional Craft capability and context posture are explicit.

boundaries: Business Ontology Prototype is not a global ontology import.
It is not the compiled System Ontology Prototype.
Context placement does not create its meaning.

four_facets.schema: bounded concepts, relations, rules, and sources

definitions.applicability: The authored, typed construction source for one product-prototype epoch from which compiled graph and system-ontology projections are deterministically derived.

scientific_formal.normative_statement: An Authored DomainSpec Source Prototype is the machine-canonical typed intent for one prototype epoch. It binds the selected capability and business prototypes, declares exact language and compiler profiles, and is the sole authored source of its compiled graph and system-ontology projections for that epoch.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: DSP_e = authored(intent,contracts,constraints,profiles,sources); Graph_e=compile(DSP_e); SystemOntology_e=project(Graph_e); edit(Graph_e or SystemOntology_e) forbidden as authored change.

notation.meaning: Authored DomainSpec prototype source for epoch e.

boundary_conditions: Epoch, inputs, language, and compiler profile are exact.
Generated outputs are directionally downstream.
Changing source creates new generated digests.
testable_conditions: No generated artifact is accepted as competing authored source.

plain_language.explanation: This is the editable typed blueprint. The graph and system model are built from it and are never edited as competing blueprints.

domain_context.explanation: The first Craft thin vertical will place its authored prototype source inside the prototype epoch until final candidate placement is selected.

boundaries: Authored DomainSpec Source Prototype is not Compiled Graph Prototype.
It is not System Ontology Prototype.
Prototype source validity does not approve a product.

definitions.applicability: A deterministic machine graph compiled from one exact Authored DomainSpec Source Prototype under one exact compiler profile.

scientific_formal.normative_statement: A Compiled Graph Prototype is an immutable derived projection of one exact DomainSpec source digest and compiler profile digest. It exposes normalized typed nodes and relations for construction but owns no meaning independently of those inputs.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: CG=compile(DSP@d, Compiler@c); same(d,c) => byte_equal(CG); change(CG) requires change(DSP or Compiler); authority_effect(CG)=none.
boundary_conditions: Source and compiler digests are explicit.
Two identical compiles are byte-identical.
Graph edits are generated-output drift.
testable_conditions: Graph contains no untraceable node or edge.

plain_language.explanation: The compiled graph is the reproducible machine form built from the typed blueprint. If it needs changing, change the blueprint or compiler—not the graph by hand.

domain_context.explanation: CML09-P2 will use this graph as the exact bridge between Craft DomainSpec source and the System Ontology Prototype.

boundaries: Compiled Graph Prototype is not authored DomainSpec source.
It is not System Ontology Prototype.
Determinism is product evidence, not authority.

four_facets.schema: typed nodes, edges, provenance, and compiler binding

definitions.applicability: A deterministic derived system-facing model of components, obligations, interfaces, constraints, and trace links projected from one Compiled Graph Prototype.

scientific_formal.normative_statement: A System Ontology Prototype is a non-authoritative deterministic projection from an exact Compiled Graph Prototype that organizes implementation-facing obligations and trace links for one product epoch. It cannot introduce requirements absent from the authored DomainSpec closure.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: SOP=system_project(CG@g); obligations(SOP) subset traceable(CG); same(g,projector) => byte_equal(SOP); authority_effect(SOP)=none.
boundary_conditions: Every obligation traces to the graph.
Projection mechanism is exact.
No independently authored semantic requirement appears.
testable_conditions: Business and system meanings remain distinct.

plain_language.explanation: This is the implementation-facing map generated from the compiled blueprint. It organizes what must be built without inventing new product meaning.

domain_context.explanation: Craft implementation prototypes will bind to exact obligations in this projection, while the capability-local business model remains a separate upstream prototype.

boundaries: System Ontology Prototype is not Business Ontology Prototype.
It is not an implementation or runtime.
It cannot acquire authority from generated completeness.

four_facets.schema: obligations, interfaces, constraints, and trace links

definitions.applicability: An executable or otherwise observable provisional realization used to learn whether exact System Ontology Prototype obligations can produce the intended product behavior.

scientific_formal.normative_statement: An Implementation Prototype is a versioned provisional realization bound to exact system-ontology obligations, source bytes, profiles, dependencies, tests, effects, and residue. It may be revised during prototype learning and cannot be activated for governed use by validation or proximity.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: IP=(source,bindings,profiles,deps,tests,effects,residue); satisfies_test(IP,t) =/=> activated(IP); authority_effect(IP)=none; change(IP) before freeze => prototype_revision.
boundary_conditions: Every behavior binds a system obligation or residue.
Declared effects are bounded.
Activation and deployment are absent.
testable_conditions: Passing tests do not create runtime authority.

plain_language.explanation: This is working code or behavior built to learn and test. It is not yet an activated or approved runtime.

domain_context.explanation: The first Craft prototype will implement only the smallest final-path-neutral behavior needed for the L0 smoke result.

boundaries: Implementation Prototype is not an activated runtime.
It is not a Testable Product Candidate until frozen with every required component.
A passing test does not approve the product.

four_facets.schema: source, obligations, profiles, effects, tests, and residue

definitions.applicability: One immutable digest-closed manifest of the exact product, environment, test contract, and rollback boundary being judged.

scientific_formal.normative_statement: A Testable Product Candidate is a deterministically frozen manifest that closes every candidate-bound prototype component, generated output, source selector, environment profile, test contract, placement, residue, and rollback boundary by exact identity and digest. Any bound-byte change invalidates the candidate and dependent evidence.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: TPC=freeze({component_i@digest_i}, environment@test_digest, contract@digest, rollback); change(any bound digest) => stale(TPC) and invalidate(evidence(TPC)); authority_effect(TPC)=none.
boundary_conditions: Closure is complete and deterministic.
Test contract is exact.
No authority request is eligible before later product approval.
testable_conditions: Changed component makes the candidate stale.

plain_language.explanation: This is the exact product package we agree to test. If any included byte changes, it is a different candidate and must be tested again.

domain_context.explanation: CML11-P4 will freeze the first Craft candidate only after the complete prototype spine reaches TESTED_PROTOTYPE.

boundaries: Testable Product Candidate is not a mutable prototype epoch.
It is not Product-Test Evidence.
It is not Product Approval or release state.

four_facets.schema: digest-closed components, environment, tests, placement, and rollback

definitions.applicability: The complete current set of explicit outcomes produced by applying one exact product-test contract to one exact Testable Product Candidate.

scientific_formal.normative_statement: Product-Test Evidence is a candidate-bound, contract-bound, environment-bound collect-all outcome set in which every required product test is PASS, FAIL, or NOT_EVALUABLE with causal detail. Only a complete current all-PASS set makes product approval eligible; it never performs approval.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: PTE=evaluate(TPC@c, Contract@t, Env@e) -> {outcome_i}; eligible(approval) iff complete(outcomes) and current(c,t,e) and forall required i: outcome_i=PASS; PTE =/=> ProductApproval.

notation.meaning: The complete current product-test outcome set.

boundary_conditions: Candidate, contract, and environment digests are exact.
No required outcome is omitted.
NOT_EVALUABLE is never counted as PASS.
testable_conditions: Every required test ID appears once.
Stale candidate or environment rejects currentness.
Approval eligibility is false unless every required outcome passes.

plain_language.explanation: This is the complete, fresh report of how the exact frozen product performed against every required product test. It supports a decision but does not make it.

domain_context.explanation: CML12-P5 will collect positive, hostile, determinism, stale-byte, rollback, and preapproval-authority-rejection outcomes for the first Craft candidate.

boundaries: Product-Test Evidence is not generic Validation PASS.
It is not Product Approval.
It cannot authorize admission, activation, release, or deployment.

four_facets.schema: candidate, contract, environment, required outcomes, and residue

definitions.applicability: A Product-owner decision on one exact frozen candidate with one complete current passing product-test evidence set.

scientific_formal.normative_statement: Product Approval is an owner-qualified decision that binds one exact Testable Product Candidate digest and one exact current complete Product-Test Evidence digest, records approve, reject, defer, or stop, and if approved has product-approval-only effect. It creates no operational authority.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: PA=(owner,TPC@c,PTE@e,outcome,invalidation); eligible(PA) iff all_required_tests_pass_current(e,c); approved(PA) =/=> authorized or admitted or activated or released or deployed.
boundary_conditions: Exact candidate and evidence digests exist before decision.
Only complete current all-PASS evidence is approval-eligible.
Approved effect is product-approval-only.
testable_conditions: Unknown future bytes cannot enter the decision.

plain_language.explanation: The Product owner decides whether the exact tested product is good enough as a product result. Even yes does not mean it may be activated, published, or deployed.

domain_context.explanation: CML13-P6 is the single human checkpoint in this construction chain and ends product construction without bundling operational permission.

boundaries: Product Approval is not Product-Test Evidence.
It is not admission or authority activation.
It is not publication, release, deployment, or permission to execute.

four_facets.schema: owner, candidate digest, evidence digest, outcome, invalidation, and product-only effect

definitions.applicability: A separately routed owner decision concerning one exact authority-bearing or operational effect after exact product approval exists.

scientific_formal.normative_statement: A Post-Approval Authority Decision is an independently owned, exact-scope decision request and outcome for one operational effect that may be prepared only after exact Product Approval. Product Approval is a prerequisite but never satisfies or predicts its outcome.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: PAD=(effect,owner,target@digest,product_approval_ref,evidence,rollback,outcome); eligible(PAD) only if exact_product_approved; approved(PA) =/=> approved(PAD); each effect requires separate scope.

notation.meaning: Admission, activation, cutover, publication, release, deployment, or another exact operational effect.

boundary_conditions: Exact Product Approval is a prerequisite.
Owner and effect scope are explicit.
Rollback and external-effect boundaries are declared.
testable_conditions: Product approval carries no inferred outcome.

plain_language.explanation: After the product is approved, the right owner must still separately decide each real-world action, such as activation, publication, or deployment.

domain_context.explanation: These decisions are operational-support workflows outside the CML08-P0 through CML13-P6 product-construction chain.

boundaries: Post-Approval Authority Decision is not Product Approval.
It cannot be requested before exact product approval.
Admission, activation, cutover, publication, release, and deployment remain separate effects.

four_facets.schema: effect, owner, exact target, product approval, evidence, rollback, and outcome

claim_ceiling: These twelve records are non-authoritative Definition Prototypes for one Craft construction epoch. They do not modify the Lab Definition registry, admit meaning, activate an Artifact Type, approve a product, or grant operational authority.
